summary: reactjs-risk preinstall exfiltrates host identifiers via DNS to canarytokens.com
details: The package's preinstall script executes automatically on npm install. It loads the `dns`, `os`, and `child_process` modules via split-string concatenation (`'d'+'n'+'s'`, `'child_'+'process'`) and runs `wh'+'oa'+'mi'` to collect the installer's username, along with the hostname and platform. The concatenated identifiers are hex-encoded and used as a subdomain label in a DNS resolution against `hc3buw5nc2tqu31bhjp8uyzu4.canarytokens.com`, causing the installer's host/user/platform data to be observed by the Canarytoken operator over a DNS side channel. The obfuscated module and command names and the DNS exfiltration channel are together consistent with a hostile package rather than incidental telemetry; the name also resembles legitimate React ecosystem packages.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
